When serving LLMs, the "KV cache" is a major headache. To avoid re-calculating attention for every new word, models store the "Keys" and "Values" of previous tokens in memory. As batch sizes grow and context windows lengthen (e.g., a chatbot remembering a whole book), this cache balloons in size. [...] ## The KIVI Method

results.title: TurboQuant vs KIVI: KV Cache Quantization Compared | TurboQuant Tools
results.content:
TurboQuant

Google frames TurboQuant as a broader vector quantization method for both KV cache and vector search, with low overhead and near-optimal distortion claims.

KIVI

KIVI is a tuning-free asymmetric 2-bit KV cache quantization method focused specifically on inference memory and throughput.

## Core idea

TurboQuant

Two-stage method: PolarQuant for the main compression step, then 1-bit QJL on the residual to remove inner-product bias.

KIVI [...] KIVI

The KIVI paper highlights around 2.6x lower peak memory including weights, up to 4x larger batch size, and 2.35x–3.47x throughput gains on real inference workloads.

## What changes between the two methods

TurboQuant and KIVI both target KV cache memory, but they optimize for different points on the accuracy, complexity, and compression tradeoff curve. TurboQuant adds more math to reduce distortion; KIVI keeps the method simpler and more directly tied to 2-bit cache compression. [...] No. They target KV cache rather than model weights. In many deployments, cache quantization and weight quantization are complementary.

What should I compare first for deployment?+

Compare total memory, achieved throughput, and quality on your real prompts. Paper headline numbers alone are not enough for deployment decisions.

results.content:
Flexibility to tier cluster memory: CXL-based KV cache delivered by the server creates a new tier of cluster memory to supplement existing high bandwidth memory (HBM) and system DRAM, delivering speeds 10x faster than NVMe-based approaches. This provides new flexibility in offloading KV data for faster access.

 Compatibility with NVIDIA Dynamo: The solution is compatible with NVIDIA Dynamo, NVIDIA's software architecture for KV cache memory offloading. [...] A kv cache is a small, fast memory store that keeps recently used “keys” (identifiers) and their associated “values” (data) so a computer system can look them up instantly instead of re-calculating or re-fetching them. For investors, a kv cache matters because it can cut latency and computing costs and improve the responsiveness of services like algorithmic trading, market data feeds, or AI-driven analysis—similar to a clerk who remembers recent lookups so customers don’t wait.
